prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right choice depends on your age, budget, health needs, whether you want ACA marketplace plans (with premium subsidies), off‑exchange plans, short‑term coverage, or a small‑employer solution (QSEHRA/ICHRA). That said, here’s a practical way to find the best broker in Kansas City, MO for your situation and what to look for.

What to look for in a broker
- Independent broker (not captive to one insurer) so you get unbiased comparisons across carriers.  
- Experience with ACA/Marketplace enrollment and subsidy eligibility.  
- Familiarity with self‑employment options (individual/family ACA plans, association plans, QSEHRA/ICHRA, healthsharing alternatives if you’re considering them).  
- Transparent about fees/commissions (some charge a client fee; others work via carrier commission).  
- Will help with renewals, claims issues, and year‑round service (not just enrollment season).  
- Good local reviews, professional licensure with Missouri Department of Insurance, and references.

Where to search
- Online national broker platforms that work in Missouri: eHealth, GoHealth, HealthSherpa, Stride Health (good for gig/self‑employed). They let you compare plans and often connect you with licensed agents.  
- Local independent agencies in Kansas City — search Google/Yelp/BBB for “independent health insurance agent Kansas City MO” and check reviews.  
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance license lookup to confirm any agent’s license.  
- Consumer groups / local small‑business organizations or self‑employed meetups for personal referrals.

Questions to ask any broker before committing
- Do you work with ACA Marketplace plans and can you enroll me in the federal/state exchange?  
- Which carriers do you place most individual plans with locally?  
- Do you charge any fees? If so, how much?  
- How do you help at renewal time or if I have a claim question?  
- Can you estimate whether I qualify for premium tax credits and help with advance payments?  
- Can you help with other self‑employed options (association plans, QSEHRA/ICHRA)?

Next steps I can do for you
- If you want, tell me your ZIP code, age, household size, and whether you use tobacco and I’ll:  
  - find 3–5 highly reviewed Kansas City agents/independent agencies, and  
  - list a couple of national online brokers that serve your ZIP code so you can compare.

Which would you prefer — a local in‑person agent or an online broker who handles everything remotely? Provide your ZIP code if you want me to pull local options.
